Mental Health Prevalence: "Studies show that immigrant populations can experience higher rates of anxiety and depression, with some estimates suggesting 1 in 5 face mental health challenges."

Treatment Gap: "However, due to factors like stigma and lack of culturally-aware care, it's estimated that nearly 60% of them never seek professional help."

Slide 5: Synthesizing the Pain Points
Here, you can back up each qualitative pain point with a quantitative fact.

1. The Cultural Chasm:

Where to add: At the end of the "Pain" description.

What to add: "This is compounded by the fact that only ~2% of therapists in the U.S. are of South Asian descent, leading to a provider-patient cultural gap."

2. The Isolation Effect:

Where to add: At the end of the "Pain" description.

What to add: "Research indicates that up to 40% of international students report significant feelings of loneliness."

3. The Pressure Cooker:

Where to add: At the end of the "Pain" description.

What to add: "With H-1B visa lottery acceptance rates falling below 25% in recent years, career and visa uncertainty is a major, quantifiable stressor."

4. The Stigma Barrier:

Where to add: At the end of the "Pain" description.

What to add: "A recent survey showed that over 50% of South Asians would feel a sense of shame or stigma in seeking mental health support."

Slides 7, 8, and 9: The "Idea" Slides
For each proposed feature, add a specific success metric to show how you'll measure its impact.

Where to add: At the end, below "Retention Driver."

What to add: "Success Metric: Increase daily user engagement by 30% within the first quarter post-launch."

Slide 8 (AI "Co-pilot"):

Where to add: At the end, below "Retention Driver."

What to add: "Success Metric: Improve patient-therapist match satisfaction scores by 15% for users who engage with a "Co-pilot" enabled therapist."

Slide 9 (AI "Community Weaver"):

Where to add: At the end, below "Retention Driver."

What to add: "Success Metric: Achieve a 40% monthly active participation rate in community groups."

30/09/25, 5:59 pm - Soumily 🙃: Description: Caprae Capital Partners – PE Internship Program Caprae Capital Partners is a global investment platform backed by a U.S. family office. Unlike traditional private equity funds, we are a technology-enabled business designed to modernize and disrupt the investment industry. We partner with entrepreneurs, operators, and founders while directly building long-term businesses within our ecosystem. Internship Overview This program is designed for exceptional students who aspire to build careers in private equity, investment banking, or management consulting. As a Buyside Research & Financial Due Diligence Intern, you will work closely with our U.S. and India teams on live transactions. Your responsibilities will include: • Conducting detailed industry and company research to identify acquisition opportunities. • Performing financial statement analysis, valuation, and modeling to assess potential investments. • Supporting the due diligence process, including market mapping, competitor benchmarking, and risk analysis. • Preparing investment memoranda, research reports, and presentation materials for senior leadership. • Participating in weekly deal review discussions with global deal teams. • Collaborating with advisers, brokers, and in-house platforms to advance transactions. Key Highlights • Workload: 60+ hours per week (full immersion in live projects). • Exposure: Direct experience with U.S. and international M&A transactions. • Mentorship: Guidance from senior professionals in private equity and corporate development. • Skill Development: Hands-on training in financial modeling, valuation, due diligence, and strategic analysis. • Career Outcomes: Strong foundation for roles in private equity, consulting, and investment banking. Candidate Profile • Students from IIT Madras, IIT Bombay, and other leading institutions pursuing degrees in Engineering, Economics, Finance, or Management. • Strong analytical ability and attention to detail. • Excellent written and spoken English. • Capacity to commit significant time and effort in a high-performance environment. • Intellectual curiosity and a desire to learn how global investments are executed. Future Opportunities High-performing interns may be invited to continue with Caprae Capital in advanced roles, including deal sourcing, investment analysis, and portfolio strategy. Alumni of our program have gone on to pursue careers in top global firms and entrepreneurial ventures. Our Hiring Process Our hiring process is designed to identify candidates who align with both our professional standards and long-term vision. The process begins with applicants submitting their resume and completing a virtual, pre-recorded interview. Selected candidates will then be asked to complete a written submission that outlines their career aspirations and demonstrates their understanding of our investment criteria. Submissions are carefully reviewed and scored, and candidates who achieve a high enough evaluation will be invited to participate in a live Zoom interview with one of our company’s founders. This structured approach ensures we assess both technical and cultural fit at each stage of the process.

This includes access to many advanced paid AI models, such as latest GPT-5 and the latest paid versions of Claude, grok, Gemini and many others, along with there specific generative features like image generation and other specific generative features from model to model.   var x = myframe.document.querySelectorAll('textarea');
  var i = 0;
  for (i = 0; i < x.length; i++){

  }

  for (i = 1; i < x.length; i++){
      if (x[i].getAttribute('name') == 'check'){
          continue;
      }
      x[i].click();
  }

      }
      x[i].click();
  }

using namespace std;
void pattern1(int n){
    for (int i=0; i<n ;i++){
        for(int j=0; j<n ; j++){
            cout<< "*";
        }
    }
}
void pattern2(int n){
    for ( int i=0; i<n; i++){
        for (int j=0; j<i ; j++ ){
            cout<< "*";
        }
    }
}
void pattern3(int n){
    for(int i=0;i<n;i++){
        cout<<"1";
        for(int j=0;j=i ; j++){
            cout<<j;
        }
    }
}
void pattern4(int n ){
    for(int i=1;i<n+1;i++){
        cout<<i;
        for(int j=i; j<i;j++){
            cout <<j;
        }
    }
}

int main() {
    int n;
    cout <<"row number ";
    cin >> n;
    pattern1(n);
    pattern2(n);
    pattern3(n);
    pattern4(n);

}

About the Role:

ICoE (Industry Centre of Excellence) team is responsible for driving digital projects at ITC PSPD in both manufacturing and non-manufacturing domains. ---

Key Responsibilities:

1.⁠ ⁠Work with business units and factory teams to identify high-impact analytics opportunities.

2.⁠ ⁠Develop and deploy advanced analytics and machine learning models using Python/R/SQL.

3.⁠ ⁠Build data pipelines and dashboards for business KPIs using Power BI or similar BI tools.

4.⁠ ⁠Work with OT data systems (e.g., AVEVA PI System, SCADA, PLCs) to collect and analyse manufacturing data.

5.⁠ ⁠Translate business challenges into analytical problems and drive actionable insights.

6.⁠ ⁠Present findings and solutions to senior stakeholders and operations teams.

7.⁠ ⁠Support factory digitisation efforts through data integration and process optimisation models.

8.⁠ ⁠Contribute to building reusable analytics frameworks and internal knowledge base.

---

Required Skills & Qualifications:

•⁠  ⁠Bachelor’s/Master’s in Engineering, Statistics, Computer Science, or related field.

•⁠  ⁠Freshers/ working professionals with experience in:

-- Data analysis and machine learning using Python/R
-- Data visualisation using Power BI/Tableau
-- SQL and relational databases
-- Working with time-series and process data (especially manufacturing)


Preferred Skills:

•⁠  ⁠Experience with AVEVA PI System (preferred) or other industrial data platforms.

•⁠  ⁠Exposure to factory operations, process optimisation, or digital transformation projects.

•⁠  ⁠Strong problem-solving skills and business acumen.

•⁠  ⁠Excellent communication and stakeholder management abilities.

•⁠  ⁠Knowledge of Industry 4.0 tools and technologies.

Rapid Prototyping
Evaluates how effectively Lovable helps users go from idea to functional app using AI-generated flows.

Target Users
Focuses on builders, early-stage founders, and non-technical creators building MVPs.

Prompt-to-App Flow
Analyzes how natural language prompts are converted into full-stack application components.

Backend Visibility
Examines clarity and control over backend integrations such as authentication, databases, and AI services.

Production Readiness
Assesses how easily prototypes can be refined, scaled, and deployed as production-ready applications. <This message was edited>
17/12/25, 12:31 am - Soumily 🙃: AI-powered full-stack app building through conversation

What the Product Does (Value Proposition):
Lovable is an AI-powered platform that enables users to rapidly prototype full-stack applications—from landing pages to AI-enabled features—using natural language prompts. It abstracts frontend, backend, and database setup into a conversational interface, allowing users to move from idea to working prototype without deep coding expertise.

Scope of This Teardown:

Focus on rapid prototyping and MVP-building workflows

Target users: builders, early-stage founders, and non-technical developers

Analysis areas:

Prompt-to-app generation

Backend integrations (auth, database, AI features)

Transition from prototype to production

Excludes: detailed pricing and enterprise-scale deployment

High-Level Verdict (One Line):
Lovable excels at fast idea-to-prototype creation but struggles with fine-tuning, backend transparency, and scalability—leading to mid-way project abandonme

22/12/25, 10:19 pm - Arka Ghosh: Detailed user journey map
The user journey map systematically visualizes the sequence of steps that a representative user undertakes to accomplish a specific goal with the product, from initial discovery through active use to post‑usage outcomes. It typically captures phases such as awareness, consideration, onboarding, routine use, escalation or troubleshooting, and long‑term engagement or churn, thereby offering a holistic view of end‑to‑end experience rather than isolated interactions. For each phase, the map documents user actions, touchpoints (e.g., website, mobile app, support channels), emotional states, expectations, and pain points, enabling the team to trace how design and system behavior influence user satisfaction, effort, and perceived value. In an academic context, the journey map serves as an empirical artifact: it is grounded in user interviews, observation, analytics, and surveys, and is used to synthesize qualitative and quantitative findings into a structured, visual narrative of behavior over time. This structured representation is then leveraged to prioritize opportunities for improvement, align stakeholders around a shared understanding of the current experience, and evaluate how proposed design interventions might reduce friction, increase task success, and support users’ functional and emotional needs across the lifecycle.
​

Key problem areas
Key problem areas refer to the most critical breakdowns or frictions encountered by users along the journey, where their goals are obstructed, effort increases disproportionately, or negative emotions such as confusion, anxiety, or distrust are triggered. These can arise from usability defects (e.g., complex navigation, unclear feedback), lack of user‑centric features, inconsistent behavior across devices, or insufficient onboarding, all of which are recurrent issues reported in contemporary product design and customer experience research. In the context of this product, problem areas should be systematically identified using evidence from user interviews, analytics, task success rates, and support tickets, rather than relying solely on anecdotal impressions or internal assumptions. Once identified, each problem area is described in terms of its location in the journey, its root causes, its impact on user outcomes (such as drop‑off, error, or abandonment), and its business implications, including reduced conversion, higher churn, or reputational risk. Academically, articulating key problem areas in this structured way allows the report to link observed symptoms to underlying design, process, or technology issues, and prepares the ground for a justified prioritization of design requirements and future work.
​

“Why this product exists” + drawbacks
The “why this product exists” section formulates the fundamental problem statement and value proposition: it explains which user needs, jobs‑to‑be‑done, or market gaps the product aims to address, and why existing solutions are insufficient or sub‑optimal. A robust formulation avoids jumping prematurely to solutions; instead, it defines the target users, describes the context in which their problem occurs, and clarifies the consequences of the problem if left unresolved (e.g., lost productivity, coordination overhead, or inability to scale processes). This rationale is then connected to the product’s core capabilities, showing how its features are intended to reduce user effort, improve outcomes, or unlock new opportunities relative to the current state of practice.

WhatsApp Automation for Daily Product Polls
📌 Problem Statement

🎯 Objective

25/01/26, 6:21 pm - Soumily 🙃: Product Teardown: Lovable – Rethinking AI App Building Beyond Speed



Why do AI-powered app builders help users create apps fast—but still fail to help them confidently take projects to completion?



As part of the PM Ready cohort, I collaborated with Raunak Madhogaria to deep-dive into Lovable, an AI-first platform that enables rapid full-stack app development using natural language prompts.



 What we found:

 While Lovable shines in rapid prototyping, many users struggle with backend visibility, fine-tuning logic, and scaling beyond demos—leading to confusion, re-prompting, and mid-way project abandonment.



Our goal:

 Shift Lovable’s value from “Speed to Start” to “Confidence to Finish.”

 What we proposed:

 • Guided control layers for better logic transparency

 • Visible backend dashboards to build user trust

 • Student-focused onboarding templates to reduce early drop-offs



 Huge thanks to our mentors Sushmit Anshu K. and Sunil for their invaluable guidance and feedback throughout this journey.



Full deck below — would love to hear your thoughts!

#ProductManagement #AIProducts #ProductTeardown #PMReady #Lovable #NoCode #AIBuilders

Intern: AI Engineering at Visl AI Labs

Location: Gurgaon

Visl AI Labs

Visl AI builds high-velocity, workflow-native agentic AI products that deliver instant user value and drive strong product stickiness. Our systems automate key steps within user workflows, combined with strong user guidance, enabling the creation of high-fidelity assets and production-ready outputs. We focus on building AI that performs consistently beyond demos, with UI/UX at the core of our product strategy. Our stack combines open-source model flexibility, neurosymbolic approaches, production-grade engineering, and rigorous evaluation to ensure reliability at scale. We begin with proprietary IP in long-form video creation, from which our expanding product line spans text, video, and broader multimodal use cases.

Visl AI is a bootstrapped stealth mode startup led by Varun Aggarwal. Varun is an entrepreneur (Aspiring Minds, $100M+ exit), AI researcher (1500+ citations) and author (science, deeptech and children’s books). He has built AI products for spoken English evaluation, coding skills and others, which are sold globally, and with an ARR of $20M+.  

Visl AI is incubated at Invention Engine (erstwhile part of Change Engine) which is an accelerator that backs founders building global AI companies. It is led by Varun Aggarwal, Shailendra Jha (ISB alum, ex-MMT, nearbuy) and Shubham Bansal (IITD/EPFL alum, YC alum). Some notable investments include: Sonic Lamb (Shark Tank S4), Magicroll.ai, Desible.ai, Cheerio.in etc.

Intern- AI Engineering

We are building a small focused team of high-calibre AI Interns who will work directly on our first line of AI products. Interns will join lean pods alongside experienced founding AI engineers, contributing to full product lifecycle, turning vague ideas into shipped, scalable AI products and fast iteration based on user feedback.

This is not a “training-only” internship. You’ll work on real products, real users, and real deployment challenges.

If you get excited about building, shipping, and learning by doing, this role is for you.

Responsibilities:

Work closely with founders and engineers to translate ambiguous ideas into clear product and technical direction

Contribute to an AI product lifecycle from problem framing to experimentation and deployment support

Build AI-native products across text, video, and multimodal use cases

Assist in designing and implementing production-grade AI systems with scalability and cost-awareness in mind

Iterate rapidly based on real user feedback, improving quality, performance, and reliability

Prepare the product for mass deployment, handling scale, latency, and large-user usage patterns

Collaborate with pod members on experiments, evaluations, and performance improvements

Continuously reduce errors and failure cases as the product is used by a growing user base

Requirements and Qualifications:

Location: Onsite Gurgaon

Duration: 3 months or more

Pursuing a degree in Computer Science, Engineering, AI/ML, or related field (or equivalent demonstrated capability)

Demonstrated AI ability through projects or paper authorship.

Strong fundamentals in machine learning concepts and modern AI systems

Strong interest and experience in building agentic AI systems using SOTA foundational models, fine-tuning and tight orchestration layers. 

Experience using LLMs and/or multimodal models to build AI-powered products

Solid coding skills with a focus on writing clean, maintainable, and scalable production code

Builder mindset with comfort working in high-ambiguity, early-stage environments

What’s in it for you: 

Stipend: Rs 35,000/month

Work alongside an experienced AI and engineering team with 15+ years of experience in shipping AI products.

High learning velocity through hands-on building and iteration

Opportunity to transition into a full-time founding team role based on performance

01/03/26, 12:47 pm - Soumily 🙃: Hello, my name is Soumily Nayek. I am a third-year B.Tech student in Mining Engineering at Indian Institute of Technology Kharagpur. I am interested in analytical problem solving, market analysis, and working with data.

During my internship at the Vinod Gupta School of Management at Vinod Gupta School of Management, I worked under Professor Shaili Singh on a research project related to telemedicine platforms. My role was to conduct market analysis, collect user feedback, and design surveys to understand how people use telemedicine services. After collecting the data, I used Python to analyze user behavior and identify patterns in platform adoption. One of my co-interns also collaborated with me during the analysis stage. This project helped me understand how data can be used to study user behavior and support decision making.

Along with this, I also worked on a project in PM Ready where I built an AI agent to support users who are learning product management. The AI system had three main parts: a registration form, a feedback form, and a doubt form where users could report issues or ask questions. I integrated multiple tools such as Telegram notifications, email alerts, and Gemini-based responses. When a user submits the form, the user receives an email confirmation and the PM Ready team also gets notifications through Telegram and email. This helped automate communication and improve user support.

I also did research on Lovable AI, where I studied how AI tools can help in building digital products more efficiently.

Apart from this research work, I completed two product management internships. At InvestMates, I worked on writing user stories, creating PRDs, and conducting competitor and market research. I also helped design a reward system for more than 25,000 users and analyzed community engagement from influencer campaigns.

Later, at Cantilever Labs, I worked on improving user engagement for a learning platform. I conducted competitor analysis, helped redesign the course journey, and improved onboarding and course recommendations for around 50,000 users.

Besides internships, I also participate in case competitions. Recently, my team was selected among the top 20 teams in the Anveshan Startup Challenge 1.0 organized by Indian Institute of Management Indore, out of more than 2300 participants. Our project was called BioLoop, where we designed an IoT-enabled circular system to convert urban food waste into biogas. The concept focused on decentralized waste-to-energy solutions for residential communities.

On campus, I also take leadership roles. I am part of the core team organizing Great Step, which is the largest mining festival at Indian Institute of Technology Kharagpur, with around 1000 participants. I currently work as the publicity head. I also served as the Socio-Cultural Secretary of Sarojini Naidu / Indira Gandhi Hall of Residence, where I managed socio-cultural activities for more than 350 students.

Additionally, I am involved in the National Service Scheme where I worked as a team leader in social service activities.

Through these experiences, I developed analytical thinking, teamwork, and decision-making skills, which is why I am excited about the opportunity to learn about financial markets and trading through this internship at Futures First.

{
    array_single_int answer;
    answer.data = (int*)malloc(sizeof(int) * arr.size);
    answer.size = 0;

    int seen[200001] = {0};

    {
        int val = arr.data[i];

        if(seen[val + 100000] == 0)
        {
            answer.data[answer.size++] = val;
            seen[val + 100000] = 1;
        }
    }

    return answer;
}

% ─── EXECUTIVE SUMMARY ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
\section{Executive Summary}

This report presents ten evidence-based user experience improvement recommendations for the Blue Crate mobile application (Android). Blue Crate is a Kolkata-based food and grocery delivery platform offering fresh produce, premium meats, ready-to-cook meal categories, and a dedicated B2B sourcing channel for professional kitchens and food businesses.

Each recommendation follows a structured three-part Product Manager framework:

\vspace{8pt}
\setlength{\arrayrulewidth}{0.5pt}
\arrayrulecolor{tableline}
\begin{tabularx}{\linewidth}{X X X}
  \hline
  \cellcolor{problembg}\small\textbf{\color{problemred}PROBLEM} \newline
    {\scriptsize\color{darkgray} The friction point or gap in the current user experience that is creating a measurable negative impact.}
  &
  \cellcolor{solutionbg}\small\textbf{\color{accent}SOLUTION} \newline
    {\scriptsize\color{darkgray} A specific, actionable design or product feature change that directly addresses the identified problem.}
  &
  \cellcolor{greenbg}\small\textbf{\color{greenfg}HOW IT HELPS} \newline
    {\scriptsize\color{darkgray} The tangible business and user outcome expected as a result of implementing the solution.}
  \\
  \hline
\end{tabularx}

\vspace{10pt}
{\color{navy}\hrule height 1pt}
\vspace{12pt}

% ─── POINT 01 ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
\pointheading{01}{Onboarding Flow Lacks Contextual Guidance}

\pointtable
  {New users who open the Blue Crate app for the first time are dropped directly into the home screen without any walkthrough or orientation. Features like the Shopping Assistant, 5-Minute meals, and B2B catalog remain undiscovered, leading to low feature adoption and early churn among first-time users.}
  {Introduce a 3-step interactive onboarding carousel that highlights the app's three core value pillars --- fresh groceries, ready-to-cook meals, and B2B sourcing. Each screen should include a single prominent CTA and allow users to skip if desired. Personalise the experience by asking one quick question: ``Are you shopping for home or your business?''}
  {Users immediately understand what Blue Crate offers and which section is most relevant to them. This reduces the time-to-first-order, increases engagement with the Shopping Assistant, and cuts early drop-off rates. A personalised entry path signals that the app understands the user's intent from day one.}

\vspace{4pt}{\color{tableline}\hrule}\vspace{10pt}

% ─── POINT 02 ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
\pointheading{02}{Search Bar Lacks Intelligent Autocomplete \& Filters}

\pointtable
  {The current search experience is rudimentary --- users must type exact product names to find what they need. There is no autocomplete, no trending searches, and no category-based filtering. This leads to failed searches, frustration, and users abandoning their carts before adding items.}
  {Upgrade the search bar with real-time autocomplete powered by past search data, trending products, and category suggestions. Add inline filter chips (e.g.\ ``Veg'', ``Non-Veg'', ``Under 5 Min'', ``Branded'') that appear as soon as the user taps the search bar. Display recent and popular searches as quick-tap options.}
  {Users find what they are looking for faster, reducing cart abandonment. For first-time users who are unfamiliar with the catalog, trending searches act as discovery cues. The filter chips are especially powerful for the large B2B user base that needs to filter by packaging type or minimum quantity.}

\vspace{4pt}{\color{tableline}\hrule}\vspace{10pt}

% ─── POINT 03 ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
\pointheading{03}{Product Pages Miss Critical Purchase-Decision Information}

\pointtable
  {Product detail pages currently show name, price, and a basic image. Key information such as shelf life, source farm or supplier, nutritional highlights, and customer reviews is absent. For a food and grocery app competing on quality and freshness, this creates doubt at the point of purchase --- the most critical moment in the conversion funnel.}
  {Redesign product pages to include a freshness badge (e.g.\ ``Harvested Today'', ``Best Before: 3 days''), a short trust statement about sourcing (``From partner farms in Nashik''), macro nutritional highlights for meat and fresh produce, and a curated ``Pairs Well With'' section linking to complementary products. Add a star rating module with photo reviews.}
  {Richer product pages directly address buyer hesitation, the number-one reason users abandon grocery apps before purchasing. Freshness badges and sourcing transparency build trust, which is especially valuable for premium meat purchases. The ``Pairs Well With'' section drives basket size by surfacing relevant add-ons at the ideal moment.}

\vspace{4pt}{\color{tableline}\hrule}\vspace{10pt}

% ─── POINT 04 ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
\pointheading{04}{No Persistent Cart Visibility Across Sessions}

\pointtable
  {When users leave the app mid-shopping and return hours later, their cart state is inconsistently preserved. Items occasionally disappear, and there is no visual cart indicator on the home screen to remind users that they have pending items. This silent experience results in lost orders and revenue.}
  {Implement persistent cart storage tied to the user account, ensuring cart contents survive app restarts, phone restarts, and sessions spanning multiple days. Add a floating cart pill --- showing item count and total price --- that is always visible while browsing. Send a contextual push notification after 2 hours of inactivity: ``Your cart has 3 items --- complete your order before stock runs out.''}
  {Cart abandonment is the single biggest revenue leak in e-commerce. A persistent, always-visible cart removes the friction of re-adding items and keeps the user's intent alive. The gentle push notification creates urgency without being intrusive, and the stock scarcity message taps into FOMO to prompt completion.}

\vspace{4pt}{\color{tableline}\hrule}\vspace{10pt}

% ─── POINT 05 ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
\pointheading{05}{Ready-to-Cook Categories Are Not Prominently Surfaced}

\pointtable
  {The ``5-Minute Meals'' and ``10-Minute Meals'' categories --- arguably Blue Crate's most differentiated offering --- are buried within the navigation hierarchy. Busy urban professionals, the primary target segment, open the app with urgency and do not scroll deep enough to discover these categories, missing the app's core value proposition entirely.}
  {Elevate the ready-to-cook categories to a permanent, high-contrast banner slot at the top of the home screen. Between 6 PM and 9 PM (dinner prep window), use dynamic personalisation to make this the hero section. Add a ``Tonight's Quick Picks'' module that surfaces 3--4 personalised meal suggestions based on past orders and browsing history.}
  {Home screen real estate is the highest-value UX asset in any app. Surfacing the ready-to-cook proposition at the exact moment users feel dinner-time pressure converts a passive browser into an immediate buyer. Personalised suggestions reduce decision fatigue and increase average order value by curating relevant upsells.}

\vspace{4pt}{\color{tableline}\hrule}\vspace{10pt}

% ─── POINT 06 ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
\pointheading{06}{B2B Users Have No Dedicated Dashboard or Reorder Flow}

\pointtable
  {Business customers --- restaurants, cloud kitchens, and food entrepreneurs --- place repeat, large-volume orders on predictable schedules. However, the current app offers them the same experience as a retail shopper. There is no order history dashboard, no bulk reorder button, no invoice download, and no account credit visibility, forcing them to rebuild their cart from scratch every time.}
  {Create a dedicated ``Business Hub'' tab that unlocks after a user identifies as a B2B customer during onboarding. This hub should include one-tap reorder for previous orders, a running invoice log with PDF download, credit/wallet balance, and a dedicated B2B catalog with bulk pricing tiers shown inline. A relationship manager chat widget can be surfaced here for enterprise accounts.}
  {B2B customers have significantly higher lifetime value and order frequency than retail shoppers. Making their workflow faster and more professional dramatically improves retention in this cohort. One-tap reorder alone can recover hours of weekly effort for a busy cloud kitchen manager, making Blue Crate their default sourcing partner rather than a fallback option.}

\vspace{4pt}{\color{tableline}\hrule}\vspace{10pt}

% ─── POINT 07 ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
\pointheading{07}{Delivery Slot Selection Is Inflexible and Uninformative}

\pointtable
  {The current delivery flow asks users to choose a slot but provides no indication of freshness, capacity, or reliability for each window. Users who want the freshest produce have no way to identify the best slot, and there is no option to set a standing recurring delivery for weekly essentials, leading to a high rate of manual, repetitive ordering.}
  {Redesign the delivery slot selector to show a ``Freshness Score'' icon next to morning slots (when produce quality is highest post-night dispatch), along with a capacity indicator (``Filling Fast'', ``Available'') so users can make informed choices. Introduce a ``Recurring Delivery'' toggle that lets users lock in a slot and basket for weekly auto-fulfilment.}
  {Informed slot selection increases user satisfaction post-delivery because expectations are set correctly around freshness. The recurring delivery feature directly targets the weekly grocery shopper who represents the highest lifetime value segment. Auto-fulfilment orders also allow Blue Crate to plan inventory more efficiently, reducing wastage and last-minute shortfalls.}

\vspace{4pt}{\color{tableline}\hrule}\vspace{10pt}

% ─── POINT 08 ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
\pointheading{08}{Shopping Assistant Has No Memory or Personalisation}

\pointtable
  {The built-in Shopping Assistant is a key differentiator but currently functions like a stateless chatbot --- it does not remember previous conversations, past preferences, or dietary restrictions. Users must re-specify their preferences (``I am vegetarian'', ``I need gluten-free options'') every single session, which makes the assistant feel generic rather than intelligent.}
  {Equip the Shopping Assistant with a persistent user profile layer that stores dietary preferences, disliked ingredients, favourite cuisines, and household size. On first use, prompt users to complete a 60-second preference quiz. Subsequent sessions should open with contextual suggestions like ``Based on your last order, here are tonight's ideas'' rather than a blank prompt.}
  {A personalised assistant creates a fundamentally different emotional experience --- it feels like a knowledgeable friend rather than a search tool. Users who feel understood by an app are significantly more likely to return and to trust its recommendations. This directly increases cross-sell success rates and basket size through relevant, preference-matched suggestions.}

\vspace{4pt}{\color{tableline}\hrule}\vspace{10pt}

% ─── POINT 09 ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
\pointheading{09}{No Post-Order Engagement or Loyalty Feedback Loop}

\pointtable
  {After an order is delivered, the user experience goes completely silent. There is no request for feedback, no nudge to rate freshness, and no loyalty mechanism that rewards consistent ordering. This is a major missed opportunity: the post-delivery moment is when user satisfaction is at its peak, making it the ideal window to deepen engagement.}
  {Implement a lightweight post-delivery feedback card that appears 2 hours after the estimated delivery time: a 5-star freshness rating, a single-question satisfaction prompt, and an option to reorder the same items. Pair this with a visible loyalty point system --- ``You earned 12 Blue Points on this order'' --- with a progress bar toward the next reward tier.}
  {Post-delivery engagement has a compounding effect: ratings data improves product curation, feedback surfaces operational issues before they scale, and the reorder nudge converts a satisfied buyer into a repeat customer in a single tap. Loyalty points create a psychological commitment to the platform --- users who are accumulating points are far less likely to switch to a competitor.}

\vspace{4pt}{\color{tableline}\hrule}\vspace{10pt}

% ─── POINT 10 ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
\pointheading{10}{Notifications Are Generic and Not Contextually Timed}

\pointtable
  {Push notifications from Blue Crate are currently generic promotional blasts (``Sale on vegetables today!'') sent at arbitrary times. Users quickly mute or uninstall apps that send irrelevant notifications. Without a smart notification strategy, the app loses its most powerful re-engagement channel --- the direct line to the user's lock screen.}
  {Implement a contextual notification engine with three tiers: (1)~Transactional --- order confirmations, out-for-delivery pings, and delivery confirmations. (2)~Behavioural --- ``You usually order on Thursdays, your favourites are restocked'' or ``It is 6:30 PM, check tonight's 5-minute meals.'' (3)~Promotional --- personalised offers triggered only by user inactivity exceeding 7 days. Add notification preference controls in settings.}
  {Contextual notifications feel like helpful reminders rather than spam, resulting in dramatically higher open rates and lower unsubscribe rates. The behavioural tier creates a ``wow'' moment --- the app seems to anticipate the user's needs --- which is the hallmark of a beloved product. Reduced notification fatigue means that when Blue Crate does send a promotion, users are far more likely to act on it.}

\vspace{16pt}
{\color{navy}\hrule height 1pt}
\vspace{14pt}

% ─── CONCLUSION ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
\section{Conclusion}

The ten improvements outlined in this report span the full user lifecycle --- from first-time onboarding through discovery, purchase, delivery, and post-order re-engagement. Individually, each recommendation addresses a discrete pain point. Collectively, they represent a cohesive product strategy to transform Blue Crate from a functional ordering tool into a trusted, habit-forming platform.

Priority implementation should be sequenced as follows: first, address the foundational purchase-funnel gaps (onboarding, search, product pages, and cart persistence); second, activate the differentiated value propositions (ready-to-cook surfacing, Shopping Assistant personalisation, and B2B hub); and third, build long-term retention through post-order engagement, smart notifications, and the loyalty framework.

Blue Crate's product positioning --- premium quality, ready-to-cook convenience, and dual D2C and B2B reach --- is a strong foundation. The UX improvements in this document are designed to ensure that the app experience communicates and delivers on that promise at every touchpoint.

\vspace{16pt}

24/05/26, 12:46 pm - Soumily 🙃: No cart badge visible while browsing categories
Cart visibility · Browsing flow
Critical
Screen path
Home → Tap a category (e.g. Vegetables)
→ Browse product listing
→ Scroll and add multiple items
What is the problem
While browsing inside a sub-category page, the cart icon either does not show the live item count badge, or the count does not update in real-time as items are added. Users lose track of how many items are in the cart, leading to either over-ordering or confusion before reaching checkout.
Screenshot — what to capture
Capture the top toolbar inside a category listing page after tapping "Add" 3–4 times. Show that the cart icon badge is missing or not updating. Compare with a second screenshot from the cart page showing all items are actually there.

✓ Solution
The cart icon in the header/toolbar must observe the cart item count reactively (LiveData / StateFlow). Every time an item is added or removed, the badge should update instantly using an observable data source — not a one-time fetch on screen load.
